1.title: One bolt.
1.body: Frame 1: a breaker bar already on a rusted 1959 frame or cab-mount bolt, Jacob's hand on the bar, shop light. Lockup: "67 years" / "ONE BOLT". No speech; the bar creaks, the bolt does not move, cut on the exhale. 10 to 12 s, one shot. Caption line 1: "For whoever is pulling a cab off a 67 year old frame this weekend." Footage: the frame work, whichever bolt is real that day. Backed by the row (fails are the biggest view row) and the column neighbours (Old x Roller 18, 0.97 share); MEME-ECONOMY meme 5. Day 9 morning.
1.caption_line1: For whoever is pulling a cab off a 67 year old frame this weekend.
1.frame1: a breaker bar already on a rusted 1959 frame or cab-mount bolt, Jacob's hand on the bar, shop light.

2.title: It sat in a field and now it won't.
2.body: Frame 1: wide of the F600 at 0.0, VO at 0.0: "I bought one of the last 1959 F600s left in Wyoming and it's trying to kill me." Then the actual first problem (seized bolt, rotten cab mount, the fuel line, whatever is real), cut every 2 to 3 s, Jacob's face not before 10 s, the fix, the key or the hoist at the end, "one down." 60 to 90 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy whose project tried to kill him this week." Footage: the frame swap prep, shot on the Pocket 3 on a magnet mount. DriveHub's 5.76M came from a 14k-median channel with exactly this structure. Day 2 afternoon.
2.caption_line1: For the guy whose project tried to kill him this week.
2.frame1: wide of the F600 at 0.0, VO at 0.0: "I bought one of the last 1959 F600s left in Wyoming and it's trying to kill me." 3.title: Fit on the bench.
3.body: Frame 1: Jacob's own cutout (shot on the shop's flat wall, keyed in CapCut) over a still of a bracket held against the frame, one text block top third: "Measured it four times. Fit on the bench. Does not fit on the truck. Same bracket." No speech. 6 to 8 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to the guy who measured twice and it still didn't fit." Backed by Shop x Meme (2.30 share) applied to the fails row; bluecollar.memes 17, 33. Day 10 morning.
3.caption_line1: Send this to the guy who measured twice and it still didn't fit.
3.frame1: Jacob's own cutout (shot on the shop's flat wall, keyed in CapCut) over a still of a bracket held against the frame, one text block top third: "Measured it four times.

4.title: Did it fit?
4.body: Coworker off camera: "Did it fit?" Jacob: "It fit." "...Did it fit?" "It fit on the bench." One shot at the frame, cut on the last word. 7 s. Caption line 1: "For every shop that has asked this question twice in one day." Backed by Shop x Skit (23 posts, 1.79); albertamechanic's clean versions at 2.5 to 3.5. Day 12 morning.
4.caption_line1: For every shop that has asked this question twice in one day.

5.title: 7.3 guys, the three parts you will buy twice.
5.evidence: 2 posts, Ford Boss Me; plus the counter-credential lane
5.body: Frame 1: Jacob at a counter-height bench with a CPS in his hand, "7.3 guys. Three parts you'll buy twice, in order." CPS, UVCH, IPR. Say the acronyms, do not explain them. One fact each, 25 s, no text. Caption line 1: "For the 7.3 owner saving up for the wrong thing." Footage: parts in hand, the 7.3 on the stand behind. Backed by Ford Boss Me 135 and 172, the 6.7 tribe's list-format results (Nick's Powerstroke 344k on 10k subs), and the parts-counter lane study. Day 6 afternoon.
5.caption_line1: For the 7.3 owner saving up for the wrong thing.
5.frame1: Jacob at a counter-height bench with a CPS in his hand, "7.3 guys.

6.title: Did you know about this?
6.body: Frame 1: a real clip from Jacob's own world with something going wrong or a hack happening (a load strapped the wrong way at the lot, the paperclip-on-the-relay trick from Dentside Depot done on the '59, a Marketplace truck "repair"), one white pill top centre: "WHAT WOULD YOU DO?" or "DID YOU KNOW ABOUT THIS?" Jacob keyed lower-left reacting out loud ("no way... somebody test this") for the hack version; silent for the fail version. 9 to 25 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who's been locked out of his truck in a parking lot at 6 a.m." Footage must be his own or clearly reposted with credit; no shop signage. Backed by DPP 2, 4, 6, 7; Dentside Depot 110. Day 1 morning.
6.caption_line1: For the guy who's been locked out of his truck in a parking lot at 6 a.m.

7.title: 6:02 a.m.
7.body: Frame 1: the parts counter in the dark, the first light flickers on, the phone is already ringing. One locked shot, 10 s, real sound, no text. Caption line 1: "For every parts guy whose phone rings before the lights are on." Footage: a morning at the counter, nothing identifying. Backed by Lifted Rippers 218 only; the cell is a bet. Day 15 afternoon.
7.caption_line1: For every parts guy whose phone rings before the lights are on.
7.frame1: the parts counter in the dark, the first light flickers on, the phone is already ringing.

8.title: The order that came back three times.
8.body: Frame 1: Jacob at the counter screen, VO at 0.0: "One part. Three returns. Same truck. Here's what was actually wrong." Named engine (ISX, X15, DD15), no customer, no shop name, the principle at the end ("the part was never the problem"). 60 s, cut on the screen, the box, the part. Caption line 1: "For the parts guy who has explained a core charge four times today." Backed by gearman_93 26, 205, 216 and the owner-operator finding that exact bills travel. Day 5 afternoon (the semi variety slot).
8.caption_line1: For the parts guy who has explained a core charge four times today.
8.frame1: Jacob at the counter screen, VO at 0.0: "One part.

9.title: Porch light.
9.evidence: 18 posts, median 15.2x, median share 2.30; bluecollar.memes 85x at 3.35
9.body: Frame 1: Jacob's own cutout (laughing or shrugging) over a still of the shop floor, text top third like a text message: "Got called to the office again. Apparently calling the new guy 'Porch Light' because he only works when somebody walks by isn't acceptable." No speech, 6 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to the coworker who only works when someone walks by." This is the account's own best cell (10 mil, 4.91 percent). Backed by bluecollar.memes 17, 25, 33, 46, 85 and I1. Day 3 morning.
9.caption_line1: Send this to the coworker who only works when someone walks by.
9.frame1: Jacob's own cutout (laughing or shrugging) over a still of the shop floor, text top third like a text message: "Got called to the office again.

10.title: It's a sensor.
10.body: Coworker: "What's it need?" Jacob: "A sensor." "Which one?" Jacob holds up a can of brake clean. Cut on the can. 6 s, one shot at the counter, no music, no text. Caption line 1: "Send this to the guy whose diagnosis is always 'it's a sensor.'" Backed by Lifted Rippers 44, 103, 126; joegotti 30; the albertamechanic clean versions. Day 2 morning.
10.caption_line1: Send this to the guy whose diagnosis is always 'it's a sensor.'

11.title: Parts guys, the most returned part in the building this year.
11.body: Frame 1: Jacob with the returns shelf behind him, the part in hand, "Parts guys, this one's for you. The most returned part in this building in 2026, and it's not the one you'd guess." One part, one reason, principle only. 20 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who buys by the box color." Backed by the Numbers x News column (17 posts) and the September "don't buy this" format; employee disclosure in the caption. Day 11 afternoon.
11.caption_line1: For the guy who buys by the box color.
11.frame1: Jacob with the returns shelf behind him, the part in hand, "Parts guys, this one's for you.

12.title: Who's this at your shop?
12.evidence: 1 post, Lifted Rippers "tag your favorite coworker"
12.body: Frame 1: a coworker doing the thing everyone's coworker does (opening a third energy drink, carrying one bolt across the shop, standing in the bay door), one pill: "WHO'S THIS AT YOUR SHOP?" No speech, 8 s. Caption line 1: "Every shop has this guy. This one's for him." Backed by 150 and the DDC energy-drink nature doc (6.89 percent). Day 8 morning.
12.caption_line1: Every shop has this guy. This one's for him.
12.frame1: a coworker doing the thing everyone's coworker does (opening a third energy drink, carrying one bolt across the shop, standing in the bay door), one pill: "WHO'S THIS AT YOUR SHOP?" No speech, 8 s.

13.title: Your boyfriend's dream truck, 1959 edition.
13.body: Frame 1: the '59 cab at golden hour, the Ford script, the handheld walk starts moving at 0.0. Silent, ambient only, no text, 25 to 30 s, one take: door latch, the lettering, the dash, the Super Duty frame beside it. Caption line 1: "For the girl whose boyfriend keeps sending her old Fords." Backed by 45, 34, 106, 16 (walkarounds with nothing on screen). Day 4 afternoon.
13.caption_line1: For the girl whose boyfriend keeps sending her old Fords.
13.frame1: the '59 cab at golden hour, the Ford script, the handheld walk starts moving at 0.0.

14.title: There's a kid in Cheyenne doing his first 7.3.
14.body: Frame 1: Jacob at the bench, "There's a kid in Cheyenne trying to do his first 7.3 and he's stuck on the exact thing I was stuck on." 30 s, two 2 s inserts of the part in question, ends on "should I go help him?" Part two three days later. Caption line 1: "For anyone who learned this stuff from a stranger." Only if the kid is real; otherwise swap for the "why it stays 2WD" reply-to-comment reel. Backed by 67 and 119. Day 14 afternoon.
14.caption_line1: For anyone who learned this stuff from a stranger.
14.frame1: Jacob at the bench, "There's a kid in Cheyenne trying to do his first 7.3 and he's stuck on the exact thing I was stuck on." 30 s, two 2 s inserts of the part in question, ends on "should I go help him?" Part two three days later.

15.title: 7.3 owners when someone asks how fast it is.
15.evidence: 15 posts, median 10.6x; bensdiesels 4.72 and 2.79, dreadlock boxer 47x
15.body: Frame 1: Jacob's own cutout, deadpan, over the 7.3 on the stand, text: "7.3 owners when someone asks how fast it is: 'it's not about that.'" Second card at 0:04: "550 to 600 on compounds. It is a little about that." 8 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to your 7.3 brother." Backed by 53, 49, 31, 125, 214 (Power Hungry's 7.3 memes share at 3.6 to 3.9 on a 1.4k-median page). Day 5 morning.
15.frame1: Jacob's own cutout, deadpan, over the 7.3 on the stand, text: "7.3 owners when someone asks how fast it is: 'it's not about that.'" Second card at 0:04: "550 to 600 on compounds.

16.title: Nice Cummins.
16.body: At the fuel island or the lot, Jacob walks up to a parked Powerstroke and tells its owner (a coworker) "nice Cummins." The owner just looks at him. 6 s, cut on the look. Caption line 1: "Send this to the guy who calls every diesel a Cummins." Backed by Shop x Skit and MEME-ECONOMY meme 4. Day 11 morning.
16.caption_line1: Send this to the guy who calls every diesel a Cummins.

17.title: 7.3 guys, this one's for you.
17.evidence: empty on TikTok; the BREAKDOWN's top-sharing build format
17.body: Frame 1: Jacob beside the engine, first line: "7.3 guys, this one's for you." The fact: it is an OBS-era core built with the 99 to 03 fuel and electronics package, HPOP, IDM, PCM and harness, mechanical lift pump drive blocked off on the front cover. Both halves of the tribe get their engine. 20 s, no text. Caption line 1: "For the one who still says OBS or Super Duty, pick one." Backed by DDC 50 (2.25 percent), FASS 136 (2.95) and the tribe report opener 1. Day 1 afternoon.
17.caption_line1: For the one who still says OBS or Super Duty, pick one.
17.frame1: Jacob beside the engine, first line: "7.3 guys, this one's for you." The fact: it is an OBS-era core built with the 99 to 03 fuel and electronics package, HPOP, IDM, PCM and harness, mechanical lift pump drive blocked off on the front cover.

18.title: Guess the truck by the door.
18.evidence: 7 posts across 7 accounts; c10talk 73x, bensdiesels learn-to-fly 3.15, DPP Imagine 4.4
18.body: Frame 1: Jacob's hand already on the '59 door, one pill top centre: "GUESS THE TRUCK BY THE DOOR." Three static medium shots: the 1959 door slam (that hollow clang), label 1959; Chief's door, 2011; a new aluminum Super Duty door at the lot, 2024. 10 s, real sound only. Caption line 1: "For the guy who says they don't build them like they used to." Backed by Lifted Rippers Y5 (21.4M on a 20k channel), 19, 54, 114. Day 3 afternoon.
18.caption_line1: For the guy who says they don't build them like they used to.
18.frame1: Jacob's hand already on the '59 door, one pill top centre: "GUESS THE TRUCK BY THE DOOR." Three static medium shots: the 1959 door slam (that hollow clang), label 1959; Chief's door, 2011; a new aluminum Super Duty door at the lot, 2024.

19.title: DEAL LUMBER & CONST. CO., LARAMIE, WYO.
19.evidence: 18 posts, median 11.1x; Squarebody Syndicate 41x at 2.39, jeff.salv 27x at 1.64
19.body: Frame 1: the door lettering, close, the phone turning the handheld walk at 0.0. Silent detail walk: the lettering, FR-5-4866, the door latch, the dash, the F600 badge, the hood ornament, one wide at the end. 30 s, no text, one take, song added in-app (the Seger clip did 1.9 for dom_obs7.3). Caption line 1: "Send it to whoever still talks about grandpa's Ford." Backed by 35, 55, 70, 71, 15 and 19 (interior and detail walks with nothing on screen). Day 4 morning.
19.caption_line1: Send it to whoever still talks about grandpa's Ford.
19.frame1: the door lettering, close, the phone turning the handheld walk at 0.0.

20.title: This truck worked for a lumber company in 1959.
20.body: Frame 1: the truck wide, VO at 0.0: "This truck hauled lumber out of Laramie, Wyoming starting in 1959. Here's what 67 years did to it." A walk through the damage with the story: the cab, the rot, the 2WD, the frame that is leaving, the lettering that gets photographed before paint. Cut every 2 to 3 s, 60 to 75 s, captions for the first 20 s only. Caption line 1: "For the guy restoring his grandpa's truck one bolt at a time." Backed by 8, 160, 215 and the Oversteer Y9 read. Day 7 afternoon.
20.caption_line1: For the guy restoring his grandpa's truck one bolt at a time.
20.frame1: the truck wide, VO at 0.0: "This truck hauled lumber out of Laramie, Wyoming starting in 1959.

21.title: It's all original.
21.body: Frame 1: Jacob with a hand on the cab, text card "it's all original" (LOUDER lockup), 2 s; the phone pans down to the Super Duty frame and the modern suspension mounts, 5 s; back to his face, cut. Caption line 1: "Send this to the purist in your group chat. He is not going to like it." Backed by the Old row (34 outliers) and the meme column; MEME-ECONOMY meme 14; the 57 to 60 tribe's "leave the '59 alone" reflex. Day 13 afternoon (the one meme in an afternoon slot, because the week's afternoons are otherwise all talking reels).
21.caption_line1: Send this to the purist in your group chat. He is not going to like it.
21.frame1: Jacob with a hand on the cab, text card "it's all original" (LOUDER lockup), 2 s; the phone pans down to the Super Duty frame and the modern suspension mounts, 5 s; back to his face, cut.

22.title: Numbers matching?
22.body: Buddy: "What year?" Jacob: "Fifty-nine." "Original?" "The cab is." "...And?" "That's it." One shot in front of the cab, cut on "that's it." 8 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who asks 'numbers matching?' at every show." Backed by Shop x Skit and the classic tribe's purist argument. Day 14 morning.
22.caption_line1: For the guy who asks 'numbers matching?' at every show.

23.title: 57 to 60 Ford guys, I know what you're thinking.
23.evidence: 4 posts; Dentside Depot "Ford trucks were brilliant in the 1970s" 6.2x, "screwdriver and paperclips" 12.6x on 552k
23.body: Frame 1: the hater quote on screen, "Leave the '59 alone", Jacob reading it off his phone. Then the facts: only the cab and front sheet metal survive, the 1959 frame is retired and goes to the 57 to 60 group with the original running gear if they want it, 1959 was the first year Ford built its own 4x4 and this one left the factory 2WD and stays 2WD. 25 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who told you to keep it stock." Backed by 234, 266, 110 and the Stradman "keep it stock" tease (BREAKDOWN 04). Day 8 afternoon.
23.caption_line1: For the guy who told you to keep it stock.
23.frame1: the hater quote on screen, "Leave the '59 alone", Jacob reading it off his phone.

24.title: Anyone seen a '59 F600 on the road lately?
24.evidence: 1 post, Oversteer "anyone ever seen one on the road?"
24.body: Frame 1: the cab on the hoist or beside the frame, one pill: "WHEN DID YOU LAST SEE ONE OF THESE ON THE ROAD?" Silent, 10 s. Caption line 1: "For the medium-duty guys who ran one of these for a living." Backed by 231 and the F600 question the tribes ask first (what is in it now). Day 10 afternoon.
24.caption_line1: For the medium-duty guys who ran one of these for a living.
24.frame1: the cab on the hoist or beside the frame, one pill: "WHEN DID YOU LAST SEE ONE OF THESE ON THE ROAD?" Silent, 10 s.

25.title: Pyro and boost, no talking.
25.evidence: 2 posts; bensdiesels chassis twist 8.18 percent, the highest clean share in the pull
25.body: Frame 1: the ISSPRO pyro and boost on Chief at idle, Jacob's hand on the shifter, then the pull: needles move, real sound only, 10 s, nothing on screen. Caption line 1: "For the guy running compounds with no pyro." On the 7.3 later: the same shot on first fire. Backed by 95 and 192 (a number happening on camera, no words). Day 6 morning.
25.caption_line1: For the guy running compounds with no pyro.
25.frame1: the ISSPRO pyro and boost on Chief at idle, Jacob's hand on the shifter, then the pull: needles move, real sound only, 10 s, nothing on screen.

26.title: What the frame swap has cost so far, to the dollar.
26.evidence: 9 posts; DriveHub $59 paint 271x, Sharpie Corvette 86x, Kory Willis transparency 18x
26.body: Frame 1: a stack of real receipts on the frame rail, VO at 0.0: "Everybody posts the build. Nobody posts the bill. Here's the frame swap so far, to the dollar." The frame, the dead axle, the fab consumables, the stuff bought twice; running total card updated three times (the one text exception, it is the content). 60 s. Caption line 1: "For the person who wants the number nobody posts." Backed by 3, 16, 82, 204 and the growth-study gap (nobody in the twelve filled the ledger). Day 12 afternoon.
26.caption_line1: For the person who wants the number nobody posts.
26.frame1: a stack of real receipts on the frame rail, VO at 0.0: "Everybody posts the build.

27.title: Where the 10 mil at, part 2.
27.evidence: 6 posts, median 43.1x, the highest median in the matrix; tire ban 89x, BD gas 76x at 1.87
27.body: Frame 1: a still of the bare Super Duty frame beside the '59 cab, LOUDER lockup: "sponsors: 'send us the build budget'" / 0:04 "THE BUILD BUDGET:" over the frame on jack stands, Jacob's own cutout shrugging. 7 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who thinks SEMA builds pay for themselves." The account's own record cell (I1, 4.91 percent). Backed by 14, 18, 28, 39, I1. Day 7 morning.
27.caption_line1: For the guy who thinks SEMA builds pay for themselves.
27.frame1: a still of the bare Super Duty frame beside the '59 cab, LOUDER lockup: "sponsors: 'send us the build budget'" / 0:04 "THE BUILD BUDGET:" over the frame on jack stands, Jacob's own cutout shrugging.

28.title: Promise you won't get mad?
28.evidence: 4 posts; Lifted Rippers 122x "promise you won't get mad"
28.body: Jacob to a coworker (or Abby, off camera): "Promise you won't get mad?" "...What did you buy." "A turbo." "Which one." "...The second one." Cut on "second." 10 s, one shot at the parts shelf. Caption line 1: "For whoever has a 'promise you won't get mad' part in the garage right now." Backed by 10, 91, 133. Day 15 morning.
28.caption_line1: For whoever has a 'promise you won't get mad' part in the garage right now.

29.title: What it costs to put a truck at SEMA when you are nobody.
29.evidence: 17 posts, median 16.7x; BD SEMA booth 91x at 1.79, FASS Mongoose 66x, DDC 3rd Gen 2.25, FASS 2,000 hp 2.95
29.body: Frame 1: Jacob with the SEMA 2027 dates, pop numbers in the BD style, spoken from 0.0: "You cannot just drive your truck to SEMA. Here's what it actually takes." Facts from the pitches report: every vehicle must be owned or sponsored by an exhibitor; feature-vehicle space $499 to $599, applied by the sponsor around July 30 and paid by August 6, 2027; non-exhibitor logos capped at two marks of 50 square inches; booth carpet alone cost BD $15,000. 40 s. Caption line 1: "For the guy who thinks you just drive your truck to SEMA." Backed by 12, 20, 41, 50, 136. Day 9 afternoon.
29.caption_line1: For the guy who thinks you just drive your truck to SEMA.
29.frame1: Jacob with the SEMA 2027 dates, pop numbers in the BD style, spoken from 0.0: "You cannot just drive your truck to SEMA.

30.title: What are you paying for diesel?
30.evidence: 3 posts; "what MPG are you getting towing", DPP "who wants one"
30.body: Frame 1: the pump screen on Chief's fill-up, the total, one pill: "WHAT'S DIESEL WHERE YOU ARE?" and the Cheyenne price in the caption. Silent, 8 s. Caption line 1: "For everyone who just filled a 48 gallon tank and felt it." Backed by 226, 78, 18 (gas-price question clips) and BD 18 at 1.87. Day 13 morning.
30.caption_line1: For everyone who just filled a 48 gallon tank and felt it.
30.frame1: the pump screen on Chief's fill-up, the total, one pill: "WHAT'S DIESEL WHERE YOU ARE?" and the Cheyenne price in the caption.

31.title: One of the last 1959 F600s in Wyoming, and it won't start.
31.body: Frame 1: the F600 at the house, Jacob's hand on the door, VO at 0.0: "This is one of the last 1959 Ford F600s left in Wyoming and it has not run since the lumber company parked it." The whole first attempt to start or move it, every problem in order, the fix for each, the face not before 20 s, the moment it rolls or fires at the end. 90 to 120 s. Caption line 1: "For whoever has a truck in the yard that 'just needs a battery'." Title number: "one of the last". Platform: TikTok and Shorts first.
31.caption_line1: For whoever has a truck in the yard that 'just needs a battery'.
31.frame1: the F600 at the house, Jacob's hand on the door, VO at 0.0: "This is one of the last 1959 Ford F600s left in Wyoming and it has not run since the lumber company parked it." The whole first attempt to start or move it, every problem in order, the fix for each, the face not before 20 s, the moment it rolls or fires at the end.

32.title: Frame swap, to the dollar.
32.body: Frame 1: a receipt pile on the hood, VO: "Everybody asks what a frame swap costs. Nobody posts the number. Here is mine so far, to the dollar." Every line item on screen as a chip on its word (specchips), the surprise item, the running total count-up, the line "and I have not bought the part everyone thinks is the expensive one." 60 to 90 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to the guy who says a frame swap is cheap."
32.caption_line1: Send this to the guy who says a frame swap is cheap.
32.frame1: a receipt pile on the hood, VO: "Everybody asks what a frame swap costs.

33.title: Is parts a trade?
33.body: One shot, the counter, a tech and Jacob. The tech says parts is not a trade. Jacob answers with the day: the part number with eleven digits, the core, the truck that is "the one with the hood up", the backorder with no update, the customer whose belt has been shredded since July. The turn: the tech needs a part and cannot name it. 60 s. Caption line 1: "Tag the tech who thinks parts is not a trade."
33.caption_line1: Tag the tech who thinks parts is not a trade.

34.title: A parts manager, a 7.3, and no shop.
34.body: Frame 1: Jacob in the home garage, VO: "I order parts for semis all day and I do not have a shop. This is where a 1959 Ford is getting a 7.3 that everybody said could not make power." The build so far as trouble: the frame, the engine, the hours after work, the cost, the one thing that went right. 80 to 100 s. Caption line 1: "For everyone building in a garage after a ten-hour shift."
34.caption_line1: For everyone building in a garage after a ten-hour shift.
34.frame1: Jacob in the home garage, VO: "I order parts for semis all day and I do not have a shop.

35.title: The old man who drove it for Deal Lumber.
35.body: If a former Deal Lumber driver or family can be found in Laramie, the truck meets them; if not, the lettering, the paperwork and the last registration told as a search. 60 to 90 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to the person who learned to drive in a work truck."
35.caption_line1: Send this to the person who learned to drive in a work truck.

36.title: 20,000 of you told me what engine to put in it.
36.body: Jacob reads the top comments from the swap-vote posts (Cummins, LS, Coyote, keep the gas), answers each in one line, lands on the 7.3 and why. 40 to 60 s. Caption line 1: "For the one who commented Cummins. This is for you."
36.caption_line1: For the one who commented Cummins. This is for you.

37.title: Everything the last owner did to this truck.
37.body: Oversteer's "problems from the last mechanic" shape (4.9M): the bodges found on the F600 and the frame donor, one by one, with the fix. 90 s. Caption line 1: "Send this to the guy who bought a 'fully sorted' truck."
37.caption_line1: Send this to the guy who bought a 'fully sorted' truck.

38.title: It just started doing that today.
38.body: The customer line every service writer knows, played at the counter with a coworker as the customer; the belt shredded since July, the light on since 2024. 60 s. Caption line 1: "Every service writer has this customer. Send it to yours."

39.title: What a truck at SEMA actually costs.

loop.name: Loop
how: Closed loop: the last frame leads back into the first.
A joke a stranger gets: money, pride, the wife, the boss, the thing that should not run.
No talking. Your own cutout or your own footage, never a borrowed clip.
One LOUDER lockup on the hook, nothing else burned in. Sound added inside Instagram.

skit.name: Skit
how: One shot, one coworker, played straight. The turn lands on the last line and you cut on it.
A universal work situation: the backorder, the core charge, 'it just started doing that today'.
Bank five in one lunch break. Phone or Pocket 3 locked off, no music, no text.
The ask is spoken once at the end or lives in caption line 1. Never burned in.

story.name: Story
how: Sentence one is trouble a stranger understands. A number or a regret in the title.
Your face not before 20 s. Pocket 3 on a magnet mount, voice recorded after in the cab.
Every problem in order, the fix for each, cut every 2 to 4 s. Re-hook a third and two thirds in.
Hold the answer for the last ten seconds. End within 1.5 s of the payoff. No outro.

question.name: Question clip
how: A real clip from your own world with something going wrong or a hack happening.
One white pill top centre with the question. You keyed lower left reacting, or silent.
The question is the comment splitter: it has two honest answers.
Your footage or clearly credited. No shop signage.

A.cell: Shop x Meme (Jacob's own cutout over his own still, one text block, 5 to 8 s)
hooks: Still: the returns shelf. Text: "Got called to the office. Apparently telling a tech 'the part's on the truck, the truck's the one with the hood open' isn't acceptable." Caption: "Send this to the coworker who asked where the truck was."
Still: an empty socket slot in the drawer. Text: "'I definitely put it back.'" Caption: "Send this to whoever 'definitely put it back.'"
Still: four empty brake-clean cans on the bench. Text: "Diagnosis complete." Caption: "For the guy whose whole process is brake clean and vibes."
Still: the counter phone off the hook. Text: "'It just started doing that today.' The belt has been shredded since July." Caption: "Every service writer has this customer. Send it to yours."
Still: a box labelled with a January date. Text: "Backorder update: there is no update." Caption: "Send this to whoever has been 'waiting on a part' since October."
Still: Jacob's cutout in front of a stack of cores. Text: "Core charge explained for the fourth time today. Same guy." Caption: "For the parts guy who is one core charge from retirement."
Still: a 7.3 head on the bench, nobody around. Text: "'Lift with your legs.' There are no legs for this." Caption: "Send this to the guy who lifts 7.3 heads alone."
Still: the shop at 6 a.m., lights half on. Text: "Monday problems, as left on Friday." Caption: "For everyone whose Friday self hates their Monday self."

Still: a wall of hanging airlines and a Class 8 bumper. Text: "Customer: 'don't worry about the noise, it's always done that.'" Caption: "Send this to the owner-op whose truck has 'always done that.'"
Still: Jacob holding a part number tag up to the camera. Text: "Three numbers. One part. Wrong truck. 11 a.m." Caption: "For the parts guy who has been wrong by one digit since 8."

B.cell: Shop x Skit (two people, one shot, setup and turn, cut on the last word, 5 to 10 s)
hooks: "What's it need?" "A sensor." "Which one?" (holds up brake clean). Caption: "Send this to the guy whose diagnosis is always 'it's a sensor.'"
"Did it fit?" "It fit." "...Did it fit?" "On the bench." Caption: "For every shop that has asked this twice in one day."
"You got a 10 mil?" "I had one." Caption: "Send this to whoever has your 10 mil."
"How long's it been making that noise?" "It just started today." (pan to the obviously ancient damage) Caption: "Every service writer in America has this customer."
"Nice Cummins." (silence, the look) Caption: "Send this to the guy who calls every diesel a Cummins."
"Promise you won't get mad?" "What did you buy." "The second turbo." Caption: "For whoever has a 'promise you won't get mad' part in the garage."
"Is it under warranty?" "It was." "When did it expire?" "When you touched it." Caption: "Send this to the guy who 'just looked at it.'"
"Where's the new guy?" "Which one?" "The one from this morning." "He left at lunch." Caption: "For every shop that has hired three guys named Tyler this year."
"Can you check if you have it in stock?" (Jacob looks at the shelf behind him, back at the phone) "...Let me check." Caption: "Send this to the parts guy who can see it from his chair."
"What year?" "Fifty-nine." "Original?" "The cab is." "...And?" "That's it." Caption: "For the guy who asks 'numbers matching?' at every show."

C.cell: Numbers x Named-tribe news (Jacob to camera, the tribe named in the first five words, one number, 20 to 40 s)
hooks: "You cannot just drive your truck to SEMA." (the exhibitor rule, the $499 to $599 feature-vehicle fee, the July 30 deadline) Caption: "For the guy who thinks you just drive your truck to SEMA."
"7.3 guys, here's the number nobody says out loud: 550 to 600 crank on compounds, on a bottom end built before the turbos were picked." Caption: "Send this to your Cummins buddy. He'll be fine."
"Frame swap, to the dollar, week one." (the running total) Caption: "For the person who wants the number nobody posts."
"Injector nerds: 160 split-shot to 238/80 hybrid when the target went to compounds. Too big for the street or just right?" Caption: "Send to the guy who runs 238s and daily drives it."
"6.0 guys, you'll appreciate this: ARP studs over a custom-bore Cometic MLX, no O-rings, 55 to 65 psi, before the engine ever fires." Caption: "Send to anyone who's done head gaskets in a driveway."
"Gauge guys, I heard you: ISSPRO pyro and boost go in before the compounds get fabricated." Caption: "Send to the guy running compounds with no pyro."
"Medium-duty guys, this is an F600, not a pickup: 2-ton class, duals from the factory, going to single 22.5s pushed to the fenders." Caption: "Send to the guy who ran a two-speed rear for a living."
"Laramie, this one's for you: the doors say Deal Lumber & Construction, FR-5-4866, and the FRanklin exchange dates that to the late 1950s." Caption: "Send to the oldest Laramie person you know."
"6.7 guys: a FASS does both jobs. It feeds the CP4 clean fuel now and it is already there when the power comes. Not either or." Caption: "Tag the 6.7 guy still running the CP4 on faith."

"Chip guys, Hydra or nothing? Four things changed when the target went to 600: turbo layout, injectors, tune, intake size. Rods, pistons, girdle, cam and springs did not." Caption: "Send to the guy still on a TS6."

million_checklist: Stranger test: would someone who never owned a diesel know what is at stake by second three?
One universal emotion named out loud: money lost, pride, regret, the boss, the wife, the old man who had one.
A number or a price in the title line.
The answer held to the end. First ten seconds set the trouble, last ten carry the payoff.
Length by shape: story 60 to 120 s, skit 55 to 70 s, loop 6 to 12 s. Nothing 20 to 40 s.
A question that splits the comments, in the caption or the last spoken line.
TikTok and Shorts the same day, same first line.
Move on frame 1, first noun by 0.9 s, one lockup at most, no on-screen ask, no grade, song in-app.
post_checklist: Caption line 1 names a person type and is the sentence a sender would type.
Five hashtags max, none in line 1. No follow ask. No em-dashes.
Song added inside Instagram. Upload at highest quality. No in-app trim, filter or added text.
Share to your Story with the same one line. Pin a comment that repeats the person type.
Post the same master to TikTok and Shorts today.
Log it: python -I tools/coyote.py pending add <media_id> "<label>" <posted_iso>
rules: No on-screen call to action, no outro, no fade. The share line is caption line 1, written as a person type.
One poster lockup on the hook (LOUDER, MEGANTE or TROPI). Nothing else burned in on the fast tier.
No color grade. Real footage only. Your voice only; the Kokoro scratch voice never ships.
El Coyote only on Rival content. Never the shop name. Transmission detail stays private.
Two numbers never wrong: 550 to 600 crank hp. SEMA November 2 to 5, 2027. SEMA is 'the target'.
No delete, coal or defeat-device content. No pods, bots, bought followers. No follow gates.
Judge: views at 7 days (100,000 candidate, 1,000,000 goal). Early warning at 48 h: sends per reach over 1 percent, watch over 60 percent, skip under 45.
